Five lessons from running a tiny bakery website

Posted on September 2, 2025 by Jane Doe

For three years I have been running the website of a small neighbourhood bakery. It started as a single page with opening hours and grew into an online pre-order system that handles about two hundred orders a week.

1. Static pages are enough for most things

The menu, the opening hours and the story of the bakery are plain static pages. They load instantly, cost nothing to host and have never broken in three years.

2. Keep the order form boring

Our first order form had a fancy calendar widget. Older customers could not use it on their phones, so we replaced it with three plain dropdowns and orders went up by a third.

3. Back up the database every night

Once a hosting provider lost our database. A nightly dump to cheap object storage saved the week, and it costs less than a loaf of bread per month.

The best feature we ever shipped was a text message that tells customers their order is ready.

The lesson is simple: build for the people who actually use the site, not for your portfolio.
